chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mansur al-Sayqal, from his father, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) a dish of hareesah from the hareesah of Paradise, which was planted in the gardens of Paradise, and the Houries churned it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ate it, and it increased his strength by that of forty men. And that was something Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to make His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) joyful with.

key_terms.الْحُورُ الْعِينُ: The maidens of Paradise, known for their large, dark eyes.
key_terms.بُضْعَ أَرْبَعِينَ رَجُلًا: The strength of forty men, indicating a significant increase in physical power.
key_terms.هَرِيسَة: A dish made of mashed grains and meat, often associated with nourishment and strength.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Hareesah from Paradise in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is gifted a celestial dish of *hareesah* prepared by the *Hur al-Ayn* in the gardens of Paradise, which miraculously augmented his physical strength by the equivalent of forty men. This event highlights the Shia belief in the tangible, physical miracles (*mu'jizat*) granted to the Prophet as a divine favor (*tashrif*) to delight him, underscoring the interplay between the spiritual and physical realms in Islamic eschatology.
